provision.description:
Who implements it: the harness, or Remuda on its behalf; §3.2 (D-028 §6).

Orthogonal to `state`. `supported` answers "can this be done", this
answers "by whom" — and the difference is user-visible, because an
emulated queue is held in Remuda's ledger while a native one lives
inside the harness where Remuda cannot edit it. Defaults to
[`CapabilityProvision::Unknown`] so a pre-D-028 payload stays truthful.

CapabilitySet.description:
Complete capability record; `protocol.md` §3.2. Missing capabilities are invalid.

a pre-D-028 peer still parses; "absent" is read as "not verified", never as
unsupported.

EffortEffective.description:
Effective effort, read back from a Claude assistant transcript record
(`effort` / `perTurnEffort`); D-028 §9.1.

This is the *observed* tier, never the requested one. Claude reports
`ultracode` sessions as level `xhigh` and does not repeat the workflow flag
on assistant records, so `ultracode` is `None` unless the observation path
has positive evidence (e.g. an immediately preceding `/effort ultracode`
switch the driver itself made).

ultracode.description:
Observed dynamic-workflow flag; `None` when the transcript does not
expose it (the common case).

EffortPayload.description:
EffortPayload; `protocol.md` §5.1 (D-028 §9.1).

Emitted whenever an assistant transcript record's `effort` /
`perTurnEffort` is observed. Unchanged values are deduped by the emitting
driver, so the Hub only sees edges. The UI renders from this observation —
never from the requested selection.

effective.description: The level actually observed in the assistant transcript record.

raw.description:
Native spelling read off the record (`effort` / `perTurnEffort`), kept
for diagnostics (`auto`, an unknown future name normalizes into `name`).

requested.description:
The level Remuda asked for (launch argv or an in-session switch), when
known on the observing side.

EffortSelection.description:
Native effort selection; `protocol.md` §4.1 (D-028 §9.1).

Six Codex levels (`low..=ultra`), five Claude levels (`low..=max`), and an
orthogonal Claude `ultracode` boolean. `ultracode` is `xhigh` plus dynamic
workflow, is session-only, and is never persisted as a level name. It is
independent of Codex's `ultra` level.

[`EffortName`] additionally carries the legacy `minimal` input, which maps
to `low` for Codex and is rejected at Claude, agy, and Grok launches.

Deserialization accepts the pre-D-028 shape `{index, name}` and normalizes
legacy tier **names** through [`normalize_legacy_effort`], so a stored row
or an old client keeps working. Legacy normalization is **per harness**:

| legacy `name` | harness | normalized |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `default` | any | `low` |
| `think` | claude | `high` |
| `think-hard` | claude | `xhigh` |
| `minimal` | codex | `low` |
| `ultra` | codex | `ultra` (a real Codex level; rejected by other harnesses) |
| `quick` / `standard` / `max` | grok | `low` / `medium` / `xhigh` |
| `ultracode` | claude | `xhigh` + `ultracode: true` |
| anything unrecognized | any | the harness default (`high` for claude, `medium` otherwise) |

Normalization is by **name**, never by index: the legacy tables had
different lengths per harness, so index 3 meant `ultracode` for Claude and
`ultra` for Codex. `index` on the wire is therefore ignored on read and not
written back.

InstanceScope.description:
Resource reach of one delegation node; design §2.5.

Scope narrows monotonically down the tree: a child scope must be a subset
of its parent's. An *empty* dimension means "no narrowing on this
dimension" for the dimension's parent view — a node with every dimension
empty is the universe root (the human-seated top coordinator).

binaryPath.description:
Host-absolute executable override, Node-validated; §4.1.

Absent means the Node resolves the driver's default command the way it
always has (host default, then `REMUDA_CLAUDE_BIN`, then `PATH`). The
Hub stores the string but cannot stat the Node's filesystem, so every
containment, ownership, and mode check happens on the Node and a path
that fails them fails the launch — there is no fallback to `PATH`.

binarySha256.description:
Expected digest of [`Self::binary_path`], for pin-on-record; §4.1.

When present the Node's own pin must equal it or the launch is refused,
so a caller that recorded a binary can detect it changing underneath.

Mandate.description: The inherited owner-intent chain carried by every task; design §2.5.

chain.description: Root-first chain, always ending with the owning task's own link.

MandateLink.description:
One edge of the inherited owner-intent chain.

Every delegation edge attaches the upstream's own words, so a depth-3 node
still reads the owner's original instruction rather than a retelling.

depth.description: Depth from the human root; the root task is 0.

intent.description:
The exact words given to that task by its delegator; the root link
carries the owner's original intent verbatim.

taskId.description: Task whose intent this link carries.

title.description: That task's title, denormalised for cards rendered after renames.

anchor.description:
1-based anchor number matching the `[Image #n]`/`[File #n]` token in
the accompanying text block (2026-09-15). Absent for producers that do
not number attachments; consumers then use block order.

size.description:
Stored byte length (D-027b, 2026-09-15). Used by path-reference
delivery for the human-readable `(mime, size)` line. Absent on older
frames.

commandId.description:
`command_id`; protocol §5.2 (C2). Set only when this prompt text was
delivered through a Remuda command: the Node attaches the delivering
command's id to the next matching prompt observation (the hook
`UserPromptSubmit` turn event carries it in `related_ids`, and the
transcript user record carries it here and joins onto the queued
message's node). Additive exactly like `origin`: a prompt typed
natively into the PTY has no command and serialises without this
field, which clients must read as "human typed, no command".

origin.description:
`origin`; protocol §5.2 (D-028 P3). Additive: absent from pre-D-028
producers, which is why it is an `Option` rather than a defaulted enum
— the schema stays honest about what is actually on the wire.

Who authored this record. A Claude transcript files skill bodies,
slash-command expansions, hook context and task notifications as `user`
records, so `role` alone cannot tell the human's words from text the
harness injected on their behalf. Rendering all of them as the user's
own is both duplicated and misleading, so the classification travels
with the message instead of being re-guessed by every client.

`None` means "this producer does not classify", and must render like
[`MessageOrigin::Human`]: showing one row too many is recoverable,
silently hiding what someone said is not.

oneOf.description: Explicitly create an attach pane; never invoked by tty.attach or recovery; §7.2.

ModelClass.description: Model capability class used by `TaskSpec.minClass` and the catalog; §4.2.

ModelRoles.description: Project speaks model roles, not concrete model ids; design §3.2.

effort.description: Native effort tier name when the driver supports a runtime switch.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities this session reports at runtime; §1.3 (D-028 §4.3).

Empty or absent means "no runtime report"; the static matrix stands.

claudeBg.description: Background job identity independent of the native conversation identity; §1.3.

signalTier.description:
Highest signal layer this session actually reached; §1.3 (D-028 §4.3).

Absent on pre-D-028 payloads and on drivers that never report one.
Absent is not [`SignalTier::None`]: it means "nobody said", so
[`crate::CapabilitySet`] falls back to the static driver matrix.

NativeRequestKey.description: Correlation of a native RPC, blocking hook, or absent request; `protocol.md` §1.3.

oneOf.description: RPC numbers retain their original decimal spelling and type.
This event has no native request.

ObservedEffort.description: An effort level as read off an assistant transcript record.

ultracode.description:
Observed dynamic-workflow flag; positively true after
`Set effort level to ultracode`, positively false after a plain level
accept, `None` until a verdict says either way.

ObservedRateLimits.description:
One observed Codex `account/rateLimits/updated` frame, normalized; §4.2.

The Node does not relay these frames yet (r-p6); the REST
`…/supply/events` path accepts this shape so the loop is wired end to end.

windows.description: Account/window snapshots exactly as Codex reports them.

PlacementLedgerRow.description:
One placement-ledger row; design §2.2 ⑥/§5.6.

`reasons` / `rejected` are both the audit trail and the future bot card
body — the two never diverge because there is no second representation.

hostId.description: Chosen host, when one was chosen.

instanceId.description: Worker instance bound by the placement.

projectId.description: Project slice copied for cross-project listings.

reasons.description: Positive reasons the chosen slot was chosen (the card body).

PlacementRejection.description: One rejected candidate and why; design §4.4/§5.6.

candidate.description: The candidate skipped — a host, `(profile, model)`, or other slot id.

Project.description: Thin authoritative Hub Project entity; design §3.1–§3.2.

briefRef.description: Repo-relative brief template (advisory layer lives in the repo).

homeHost.description: Host the project coordinator seat is pinned to.

members.description: Workspaces participating in the project (Space key reused).

ProjectConfigurablePolicy.description:
Configurable policy. Owner-tunable; the first four delegate-tree limits
implement design §2.5 ⑤ (depth/fan-out are policy, not schema).

allowMultipleDispatchers.description: Relax "one active dispatch holder per project".

coordinatorFanOut.description: Active children one node may delegate, overriding the Hub default (8).

maxConcurrentWorkers.description: Max concurrent workers in this project.

maxDelegationDepth.description: Delegation depth limit overriding the Hub default (3).

ProjectEnforcedPolicy.description:
Enforced policy switches. All default on; agents may never change them
(D-031 — read-only for coordinators, change requires escalation).

casAncestorCheck.description: Land requires an ancestor check + CAS.

gateBeforeLand.description: No landing without a green gate.

noOsSettingsChanges.description: No OS settings changes from agents.

workersNeverPush.description: Workers never push; landing goes through the gate.

command.description: Gate command; authority is the merged worktree's copy.

landSerialization.description: `global-cas` — verify may parallelize, land is always serialized.

ProjectGateLane.description:
One gate lane; consumed later by r-mergequeue's `--onto/--lanes`.

Placeholder for batch 1: stored and returned verbatim, not yet enforced.

ProjectHostQuota.description: Project-side capacity view of one host with capacity; design §3.2.

diskBudgetGb.description: Scratch disk budget (GiB); retire must reclaim.

hostId.description:
Host this quota describes; it must also appear (with a workspace) in
`members` for placement to select it.

maxBuilding.description: How many instances may be building at once.

maxInstances.description: Project cap, never above the host's own `maxInstances`.

portBlocks.description: Port blocks allocated to this project on this host.

ProjectLaunchDefaults.description:
Launch-relevant defaults folded into an instance create; design §3.2 / §6.

Fold priority is explicit (request body) > project > host > global, so
every field here only fills a key the request did not name.

ProjectMember.description: One `(hostId, workspaceId)` pair — the same key Space uses (D-024).

hostIds.description: Explicit candidate hosts; empty means every member host.

labels.description: Labels every selected host must carry.

enforced.description: Enforced switches; read-only for coordinator agents (D-031).

ProjectProviderRef.description: Provider reference (no secret — projects hold only a profileId; design §3.2).

ProviderOverlaySpec.description: Launch overlay the Node writes as Claude `--settings`. The token stays off this type.

baseUrl.description: Ingress base URL copied onto `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` for gateway.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for the gateway. Empty for direct.

model.description: Model written into the settings overlay and `--model`.

scope.description: `universal` or `host:<hostId>` (D-021). Omitted on the wire means universal.

ProviderProfile.description:
Operator-configured provider profile (Hub registry). `protocol.md` §4.4 / D-012.

GET never includes the auth token; only [`ProviderSecretView`].

defaultGateway.description: When true, New Session `delegation=gateway` selects this profile.

defaultModel.description: Prefill for New Session when `modelId` is omitted.

headers.description: Extra HTTP headers for the gateway (never Authorization / x-api-key).

models.description: Catalog model ids this profile may resolve.

revision.description: Monotonic revision; increments on PATCH (including token rotate).

scope.description: `universal` or `host:<hostId>` (D-021). Omitted on the wire means universal.

ProviderSecretView.description: Public secret metadata for a stored ProviderProfile. The token is never on this type.

fingerprint.description: First 16 hex characters of SHA-256(token), or null when absent.

last4.description: Last four UTF-8 characters of the token, or null when absent.

present.description: True when the Hub vault holds a token for this profile.

PtyCarrier.description: Herdr-backed PTY launch, pinned before dispatch; `protocol.md` §4.1.

backend.description: Phase 0 production PTYs are hosted by Herdr.

server.description: Resolved binary and server lifetime; no ambient default server.

session.description: Explicit Herdr session to own the new pane.

RateLimitWindow.description:
One rate-limit window — the Codex `RateLimitWindow` vocabulary (§4.2).

`appliesTo` is the field that makes fallback correct: `["*"]` is an
account/session/weekly bucket a model switch cannot escape; `["<family>"]`
is a family bucket a sibling family can dodge (§4.6).

backoffAttempts.description: Consecutive limit hits without a reset; drives the backoff ladder.

cooldownUntil.description:
Runtime: park admissions on this window until this epoch second.
Known `resetsAt` wins; otherwise exponential backoff sets it (§4.4 ⑦).

limit.description: Declared request/token budget when the user knows one.

observedAt.description: Unix-epoch seconds of the last observed fill.

resetsAt.description: Unix-epoch **seconds** at which the window resets; null = unknown.

usedPercent.description: Fill percentage 0..=100 from the latest evidence.

oneOf.description: Explicitly create an attach pane; never invoked by tty.attach or recovery; §7.2.

anyOf.description: Successful response with method-specific result type.

RpcResponse.description: A response contains exactly one of result/error; `protocol.md` §7.1.

RuntimeCapability.description:
One capability this live session actually reached, with the tier that
proves it; `protocol.md` §1.3 (D-028 §4.3).

A runtime entry outranks the static `DriverKind` matrix for the same name.
It carries its own `state`, so a session may report a capability as
`unknown` just as truthfully as `supported`.

provision.description: Whether the harness provides it or Remuda emulates it; D-028 §6.

state.description: Observed state. `unknown` is honest and stays callable-refusing.

tier.description: Signal tier that produced the observation.

oneOf.description: Cost: prefer cheap. Latency: prefer local/warm.

SpendControl.description: Spend-control panel numbers (billing-site data, never inferred); §4.2.

limit.description: Declared period limit, decimal string in the account currency.

remainingPercent.description: Remaining percentage 0..=100 as reported by the billing page.

SupplyConcurrency.description:
Account-level concurrency ceiling; §4.4 step 2 — the primitive that was
entirely missing while only host `maxInstances` existed.

max.description: Max simultaneous in-flight uses across every host; null = undeclared.

hasCredits.description: Account has a credit balance; null = unknown.

SupplyProfile.description:
Declared supply plus observed state for one provider profile; §4.2.

Every field is optional/defaulted so a user can declare as little as
"workhorse: X, scarce: Y" and grow from there. Observed runtime fields
(`state`, `cooldownUntil`, `lastError`, window cooldowns) are written by
the Hub feedback loop, never by the user.

cooldownUntil.description: Account-level cooldown epoch seconds (exponential backoff fallback).

lastError.description: Last classified supply error (429 text, structured frame, …).

ordinaryUsageAllowed.description:
Whether ordinary use is allowed; null = unknown. Per the Codex contract
this is NEVER inferred from percentages or reset times.

priority.description: User preference order: larger wins (changed often — that is the point).

reserve.description: Reserve this supply for coordinator seats.

resetWindowMins.description: Declared primary reset window length in minutes.

oneOf.description: Ordinary worker tasks may use it.
Only coordinator seats may spend it (e.g. Fable leading a loop).
A family-scoped window is cooling; sibling families stay usable.
An account-scoped window is cooling until `cooldownUntil`/reset.

Gateway-style supply with no windows the Hub can read; used only when
explicitly prioritised or once every windowed supply is exhausted
(design §8.3 open question 4).

Task.description: One row of the task ledger; design §2.2/§8.1 row 4.

blockedReason.description: Reason carried on `failed` when the worker reported `BLOCKED <reason>`.

class.description: Task class; the only scheduling judgement attached at add time (§3.4).

deps.description: Dependency edges, unlocked by a landed sha only.

landedSha.description:
Landed commit sha; set by the land/gate step — never by a worker status
bit. Dependency edges unlock from this value (§7 #8).

mandate.description: This node's task plus the inherited chain of upstream intents.

owns.description: Repo-relative path globs this task is allowed to touch; `remuda own`.

parentTaskId.description:
Parent task; mirrors the recursive delegation tree (§2.5). Absent for a
root task the top coordinator logged from an owner intent.

projectId.description: Owning project; the task ledger slice key.

TaskBudget.description: Estimated budget envelope; design §4.3. Amounts are estimates (§4.5).

maxUsd.description: Estimated USD cap (money is an estimate, §4.5).

TaskDep.description:
One dependency edge. Edges unlock only when the referenced task carries a
landed sha (invariant I1, design §7 #8).

result.description: `<result>` body when present (the subagent's final report).

task_id.description:
`<task-id>` — the background task / subagent agentId (16 hex for a
subagent, `bsl…` for a background shell command).

tool_use_id.description:
`<tool-use-id>` — the native `tool_use_id` of the launch call. Present
on 2.1.221+; older records can omit it, in which case the completion
cannot be folded onto a tool row.

TaskPin.description: Explicit pin that disables automatic supply choice; §4.3.

TaskPlacementRef.description: Where the task's worker is (or was) placed; updated from placement rows.

model.description: Model the placement pinned (pin means no auto-resolve, §4.3).

placementId.description: Latest placement-ledger row describing this slot.

TaskSpec.description:
What a coordinator submits at dispatch/instance-create; §4.3.

Carried additively on the instance create body as `taskSpec`. Only
`class`/sensitivities are LLM assignments; the rest is planner bookkeeping.

allowDowngrade.description:
Opt into picking a weaker class when nothing satisfies `minClass`.
Default false: unsatisfied admission is `deferred`, never downgraded.

costSensitivity.description: Cost sensitivity; `high` folds price into the rank.

effort.description: Requested effort tier name (validated against catalog levels).

minClass.description: Minimum model class; admission never goes below this silently.

parent.description: Parent task in the delegation tree.

taskId.description: Bound task (`tsk_…`); batch 4's ledger owns the row.

altScreen.description:
`?1049` was active when the snapshot was taken: the session is showing a
full-screen TUI, which has no meaningful scrollback, so the client must
leave the wheel to the application instead of hijacking it locally.
D-028 §4.6 — additive; absent means "not reported", not "not alt".

snapshotBase64.description: Bounded snapshot bytes (standard base64) for attach-time replay; D-016.

TuiMode.description:
Claude renderer requested at launch (D-028 §9.2).

This is intent only; the terminal snapshot's `altScreen` reports the
observed screen state after Claude applies platform and accessibility rules.

oneOf.description: Fullscreen renderer; the launch default when no preference is supplied.
Inline renderer, named `default` by Claude's settings format.

WindowSource.description:
Where a window's numbers came from; §4.1.

Observed frames update `observed` fields but never erase a `declared`
limit; `inferred` is filled by Hub-side usage aggregation (§4.5).

oneOf.description: Harness frame, probe, or screen text (429 / Codex rateLimits).
Hub usage aggregation inferred fill level.

WorkflowLive.description: The card's live line under the header; additive r-ux-w, §5.3.

agentLabel.description: Label of the currently (or last) active agent.

phaseTitle.description: Phase title of the currently (or last) active agent.

summary.description: Terminal one-line result summary, when the run has finished.

calls.description: Number of tool calls; additive r-ux-w.

latestTool.description: Last tool the agent called; additive r-ux-w timeline card.

tokens.description: Summed token usage (input + output + cache); additive r-ux-w.

live.description: Live "current phase: agent" line / terminal result line; additive.

name.description:
Script meta `name` (e.g. `review-changes`); additive r-ux-w. Absent on
producers/journals written before the timeline card.

note.description:
When phase detail cannot be provided the card degrades to a plain tool
row plus this explanation; additive r-ux-w.

totals.description: Aggregate counters for the card's summary rail; additive r-ux-w.

WorkflowTotals.description:
Aggregate counters shown on a Workflow card; additive r-ux-w, §5.3.

All values are a point-in-time snapshot: a running run's `tokens` /
`elapsed_ms` keep moving until the terminal revision.

agentsDone.description: Agents in a terminal success state.

agentsTotal.description: Total agent slots (done + running + queued). Meaningful with `total_known`.

totalKnown.description:
Whether `agents_total` is a real denominator. Dynamic scripts whose
queued calls cannot be counted statically report `false`, and the card
shows a running count without "/ total".
